subject: NovaFin evaluation plan and acceptance criteria — next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@novafin.ai>, Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@novafin.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + proposed eval plan (post-demo)

Hi Emily / Carlos — thanks again for the demo earlier. Wanted to capture next steps and a concrete acceptance frame so your SRE/ML team can start the parallel eval. TL;DR: we recommend two open variants + our Redwood-optimized baseline, run on your sample traffic, with a short rubric for semantic accuracy, hallucination, and latency.

Recap from the call:
- Primary goal: replace the existing proprietary baseline for customer-facing summarization pipeline while matching quality and cutting token cost.
- Key constraints: PII redaction on outputs, p95 latency < 400ms, and compliance with your retention policy.
- Stakeholders: Emily (AI Lead), Carlos (ML Eng), Marissa (SE), Vivek (Sales lead).

Proposed evaluation plan (first pass):
1) Models to test:
   - Open candidate A: Llama-3-70B-Chat (int8 quant) — fast, low-cost baseline
   - Open candidate B: Falcon-40B-Instruct (opt variant) — high-fluency baseline
   - Redwood baseline: rwd-infer-1 (our optimized variant for low-latency)
2) Datasets / prompt sets: we suggest you run two prompt sets we captured in the call (attached: novafin_prompt_set_v1.txt): a) short transaction summaries (~50-120 tokens) b) multi-paragraph executive summaries (~200-400 tokens)
3) Acceptance thresholds (suggested):
   - Semantic accuracy (rubric match): >= 92% on benchmark rubric
   - Hallucination rate (factually unsupported claims): <= 3% across sample
   - Regression delta vs proprietary baseline: <= 1.5% drop in accuracy
   - Latency: p95 <= 400ms (50–150 token outputs)
4) Metrics & artifacts to share back: raw outputs (anonymized), latency histograms, token counts, and a short qualitative sample for any failure cases.

Next steps we can take this week:
- I’ll share a Drive folder with the prompt sets, benchmark rubric, and a short runbook. (You can see the link below.)
- Marissa will provide recommended Redwood runtime config and quant/kv settings for parity.
- Can we book a 45-min sync for next Tue (11/24) to review initial results? Please send time windows that work.

Attachments: novafin_prompt_set_v1.txt

Thanks — happy to adjust thresholds based on your risk tolerance.

—
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@novafin.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@novafin.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed eval plan (post-demo)

Thanks Logan — this looks good and concrete, appreciated. Quick clarifications from our side before we start: 

1) Hallucination definition: when you say <= 3%, is that per-response or per-claim? For our legal team we prefer per-claim, but we can be pragmatic if the rubric defines it clearly.
2) Can you surface the SOC 2 / security checklist and the audit log availability for the private deployment? We need to include that in our procurement packet.
3) Pricing: can you provide a rough delta between running the Redwood baseline vs the fastest open quantized model (ballpark $/1M tokens)? We won’t need a firm quote yet, just a comparitive figure to present to procurement.

We’ll run the scripts against a 10k sample and report back. For the sync next Tue we prefer afternoon PST (3–5pm) but will confirm Monday.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Zhang
AI Platform Lead, NovaFin
emily.zhang@novafin.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: evaluation artifacts + config suggestions for NovaFin (do not share until Logan confirms)

Quick internal note — draft of what I’ll hand to NovaFin once Logan okays. Keeping this tight so their engineers can run in <2 days.

Included in Drive (model_benchmark_summary.pdf):
- One-page comparison: Llama-3-70B (int8) vs Falcon-40B (opt) vs rwd-infer-1
- Expected p95 latency estimates on T4 and A10: L3-70B int8 ~ 380ms; Falcon-40B ~ 410ms; rwd-infer-1 ~ 260ms (with KV cache warm)
- Quality expectations (accuracy/hallucination) with short notes on prompt engineering levers

Runbook highlights (to paste into shared folder):
- Redwood runtime suggestions: session-level KV cache enabled, dynamic batching target 64ms window, quant profile: int8-rtx for open candidates, q4f for rwd baseline (attached redwood-config-recommendations.yaml)
- Data handling: anonymize PII fields using our regex strip before sending to eval runner; provide a small guide to map their column names to our prompts.

I also added a short rubric to the Drive link (semantic_accuracy, hallucination_count, completeness_score). If Emily wants per-claim hallucination, we can record both per-response and per-claim.

Note: procurement asks — will need SOC 2 docs. Logan, if you want I can attach a short bullets doc with where to find the evidence and who owns the artifacts for Private / Dedicated options.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
